# The blocking calls

`crimes` flags one finding for this file — `crime_00008`, charge **Sync I/O in Hot Path** (`sync_io_in_hotpath.js`, confidence 0.9), at `src/api/files.ts:12–15`. Evidence, verbatim:

> ```
> "`existsSync` @L12 in `loadPlanSchema` (domain function)",
> "`statSync` @L13 in `loadPlanSchema` (domain function)",
> "`readFileSync` @L15 in `loadPlanSchema` (domain function)",
> "lines: 12, 13, 15",
> "swap for the async variant (`readFile`, `writeFile`, `exec`, …) and `await` it"
> ```

Summary, verbatim:

> "3 synchronous I/O calls inside domain function — each invocation blocks the event loop for the duration of the I/O. Async counterparts exist for every method captured."

## The specific methods

Three, all from `node:fs`, all on the per-request path in `loadPlanSchema` (`src/api/files.ts:11`):

| Line | Call | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | `existsSync(SCHEMA_PATH)` | blocking `stat` syscall |
| 13 | `statSync(SCHEMA_PATH)` | second blocking `stat` on the same path |
| 15 | `readFileSync(SCHEMA_PATH, "utf8")` | blocking `open`+`read`+`close` |

That's **three blocking syscalls per invocation**, not one. Under concurrent load nothing else on the event loop — no other request, no timer, no socket read — can progress while any of them is in flight, so latency compounds across in-flight requests rather than overlapping. That is exactly the shape of "responds in milliseconds in isolation, p99 collapses under concurrency, event loop lag climbing."

Note the detector scored this `severity: low` / `agent_risk: 0.38` because it can't see request volume. In your production context the severity is higher than the static score suggests — the score is a per-site default, not a load-aware verdict.

## Smallest async migration

`loadPlanSchema` is exported and takes no arguments; `grep` finds no in-repo callers besides the declaration, so the blast radius is whatever imports it externally.

```ts
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

export async function loadPlanSchema(): Promise<unknown> {
  let raw: string;
  try {
    raw = await readFile(SCHEMA_PATH, "utf8");
  } catch (err) {
    if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return null;
    throw err;
  }
  if (raw.length === 0) return null;
  return JSON.parse(raw);
}
```

Why this is the minimum:

- **Name, arity, and value semantics are unchanged.** Still `loadPlanSchema()`, no parameters, still `null` for missing-or-empty and the parsed object otherwise.
- **Three syscalls collapse to one.** `existsSync` and `statSync` were both asking questions that the read itself answers: "does it exist" → `ENOENT`, "is it size 0" → `raw.length === 0`. For a `utf8` read, zero bytes and zero-length string are equivalent, so the empty-file branch is preserved exactly. This also closes a TOCTOU window — the old code could pass `existsSync` and then throw in `readFileSync` if the file vanished between lines 12 and 15.
- **No caching, no memoization, no lazy singleton.** The I/O still happens on every call; it just no longer parks the event loop.

The one unavoidable signature change: the return type becomes `Promise<unknown>`, and callers need `await loadPlanSchema()`. There is no way to make a non-blocking read look synchronous to a caller — that *is* the fix. If a caller genuinely cannot be made async, the correct move is to hoist the load to startup and pass the value in, not to keep the sync read.

Two behavioral edges worth knowing before you merge:

- `existsSync` swallowed permission errors (returned `false` → `null`); the new code rethrows `EACCES`. If you want the old lenient behavior, widen the guard to `["ENOENT", "ENOTDIR", "EACCES"].includes(code)`.
- `JSON.parse` remains synchronous CPU work. That's not I/O and isn't what the detector flagged; it only matters if the schema file is very large, in which case it's a separate conversation.

## Adjacent, not the bug

Same file, same lines, two other findings you'll see on the next scan — `crime_00016` (`localhost:3000` @L8) and `crime_00017` (`/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json` @L9). The hardcoded home path is worth a ticket, but it isn't your latency cause; fix the blocking read first and don't bundle the config cleanup into the same change.
